title: Data Dictionary
description: A normalized, provenance-aware logical description of the structure (entities, fields, keys, relationships and dimensions) of the data exposed by a distribution. It is a compact, standards-aligned projection for discovery, UI and machine clients, not a lossless replacement for native schemas (JSON Schema, OpenAPI, ArcGIS layer definitions, CF/netCDF, Parquet, etc.), which remain authoritative. Consumers must ignore unknown properties: within schema version 1 the contract only grows additively. See docs/design/data-dictionary-design.md.

schemaVersion.title: Normalized data dictionary contract version
schemaVersion.description: Version of the normalized data dictionary contract. This schema accepts version 1.x payloads (initial value: `1.0`).

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: Logical record shapes contained in the distribution, e.g. a CSV table, an Excel sheet, an ArcGIS layer feature, an API request/response body, a database table or a NetCDF variable collection. Multiple entities are kept separate rather than flattened. May be empty.

relationships.title: Relationships
relationships.description: Explicitly declared references/foreign keys between entities of this dictionary. Record a relationship only when it is supported by authoritative metadata, explicit user input or reviewed evidence. Similar field names alone are not evidence of a relationship.

fieldPath.title: Normalized field path
fieldPath.description: Stable normalized schema path of a field within its entity (not an executable JSONPath/query expression). Object property segments are separated by `.`; `[]` after a segment means traversal into array items; a backslash escapes the next reserved character, so literal `\`, `.`, `[` and `]` characters in source names must be escaped. Examples: `scientificName`, `properties.location.latitude`, `items[].measurements[].value`, `a\.b` (a field literally named `a.b`).

fieldPathList.description: An ordered, non-empty list of normalized field paths. Order is significant for composite keys/references.

source.title: Source metadata
source.description: The schema/metadata source used to build the dictionary. The native schema/specification remains the authority for details the normalized dictionary does not carry.

type.title: Source type
type.description: Kind of source the dictionary was built from. Open vocabulary.

url.title: Source/native specification URL
url.description: URL of the native schema/specification/metadata document, where applicable.

documentationUrl.title: Documentation URL
documentationUrl.description: Optional URL of human-readable documentation describing the source structure.

identifier.title: Native identifier
identifier.description: Native identifier of the source schema/document where available.

version.title: Native version
version.description: Native version of the source schema/document where available.

retrievedAt.title: Retrieved at
retrievedAt.description: When the source was retrieved (ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 date-time).

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: Fingerprint (e.g. `sha256:<hex>`) of the retrieved native source structure. Used to detect source schema drift on re-harvest.

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: How the metadata was produced or curated, and its review state. Dictionary-level provenance is inherited by entities, fields, dimensions and relationships unless they carry their own `provenance` (nearest wins, no merging). `propertyProvenance` overrides apply to individual properties of a node.

method.title: Method
method.description: Origin of the metadata. Initial values: `authoritative-import` (normalized from an authoritative native schema), `harvested` (derived deterministically from source metadata), `inferred` (inferred from sampled data), `manual` (manually authored by a custodian/editor) and `agent-generated`. Open vocabulary: consumers should treat unknown values as unreviewed/advisory.

reviewStatus.title: Review status
reviewStatus.description: Review state. Initial values: `unreviewed`, `reviewed`, `custodian-approved`, `rejected`. Automatic producers must not silently overwrite manually authored or reviewed/custodian-approved values.

generator.title: Generator
generator.description: Producer/tool (and version) that generated the metadata, e.g. `magda-csv-inspector/1.0`.

generatedAt.title: Generated at
generatedAt.description: When the metadata was generated (ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 date-time).

sourceType.title: Source type
sourceType.description: Optional source type the metadata was derived from, where it differs from or refines the dictionary-level `source.type`.

sourceFingerprint.title: Source fingerprint
sourceFingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the native source structure this metadata was generated from or reviewed against. Allows a producer to detect that reviewed metadata predates a source change.

sample.title: Sample extent
sample.description: Extent of the sample used when metadata was inferred from data. Must be recorded for sample-based inference so consumers do not mistake it for complete-source authority.

strategy.description: Optional description of how the sample was selected, e.g. `head`, `random`.

reviewedAt.title: Reviewed at
reviewedAt.description: When the review happened (ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 date-time).

propertyProvenance.title: Property-level provenance overrides
propertyProvenance.description: Provenance overrides for individual direct properties of this node, keyed by property name (e.g. `description`, `semanticConcept`, `unit`). Used for mixed-origin metadata, e.g. a source-derived `type` with a custodian-approved `description`.

valueDomain.title: Value domain
valueDomain.description: Rich value domain, e.g. a code list with labels or an authoritative external vocabulary. `values` may be omitted when `uri` is authoritative and enumeration would be impractical.

type.description: Kind of value domain. Open vocabulary, e.g. `codelist`, `range`.

name.description: Native name of the domain where available.

uri.description: URI of an authoritative external code list/vocabulary.

value.description: The machine code/value as it appears in the data.

minimum.description: Lower bound of a range domain.

maximum.description: Upper bound of a range domain.

geometry.title: Geometry metadata
geometry.description: Summary of feature geometry for feature-oriented entities.

crs.description: Coordinate reference system, e.g. `EPSG:4326` or a CRS URI.

spatialDimension.description: Spatial (coordinate) dimension of the geometry, e.g. 2 or 3.

fieldPath.description: Path of the field holding the geometry, where applicable.

dimension.title: Dimension
dimension.description: A named dimension/axis of array-oriented data (e.g. NetCDF/Zarr). Physical storage details (chunking, compression) stay in native metadata.

id.description: Dimension identifier, unique within the entity. Referenced from `fields[].dimensions`.

size.description: Fixed/current size of the dimension, where known.

fieldPath.description: Path of the coordinate variable/field describing this axis, where one exists.

field.title: Field
field.description: A normalized field addressed by a stable path within its entity. Only `path`, `name` and `type` are required; all descriptive, semantic and constraint properties are optional and independent.

path.description: Stable normalized path within the entity. Must be unique within the entity and preserved across re-harvesting while the logical source field is unchanged.

name.description: Display/source field name. For flat tabular resources this is the exact source column name, even when `path` escapes reserved characters.

sourcePath.description: Native path/addressing form where it differs from the normalized `path`.

sourceIdentifier.description: Stable native field identifier where available.

roles.description: Structural roles of the field. Open vocabulary, e.g. `identifier`, `reference`, `primary-geometry`, `primary-temporal`, `coordinate`, `data-variable`.

type.description: Normalized logical type. Suggested values: `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `time`, `object`, `array`, `geometry`, `binary`, `unknown`. Use `unknown` when a useful normalized type cannot be established; consumers should treat unrecognised values as `unknown`.

format.description: Optional refinement of the normalized type, e.g. `uri`, `uuid`, `email`, `decimal`, `int64`, `geojson-geometry` or a source date format string.

semanticConcept.description: Stable URI or controlled identifier of the concept the field represents (e.g. a Darwin Core term URI or CF standard name).

enum.description: Allowed machine values when only codes matter. Prefer `valueDomain` when labels/descriptions or an authoritative code list URI are available.

missingValues.description: Values used in the data to represent missing values.

required.description: Whether the field must be present.

nullable.description: Whether the field may be null/empty.

unique.description: Whether values must be unique within the entity.

constraints.description: Additional simple source constraints that have no dedicated property.

dimensions.description: Ordered IDs of the entity `dimensions` this (array) variable is indexed by, in source order.

entity.title: Entity
entity.description: A logical record shape within the distribution (table, sheet, feature layer, request/response body, database table, variable set, ...).

id.description: Identifier, unique and stable within the dictionary. Prefer a stable source/native identifier; otherwise use a deterministic producer-specific ID. Referenced by `relationships` and by `distribution-contract` (`dictionaryEntity`).

sourceIdentifier.description: Stable source/native entity identifier (e.g. sheet name, layer id, table name, schema `$ref`) where available.

primaryKey.description: Ordered field paths forming the entity's primary key (single or composite).

constraints.description: Additional simple entity-level constraints that have no dedicated property.

entity.description: ID of an entity in this dictionary.

fields.description: Ordered field paths within the entity. Composite references list multiple paths in the same order on both sides.

relationship.title: Relationship
relationship.description: An explicitly declared reference between entities (aligned with CSVW/Frictionless foreign keys).

type.description: Relationship type. Open vocabulary; defaults to `foreign-key` when omitted.
